comments.body:
MEASUREMENT WIDENED — the asymmetry is worse than this ticket first recorded, found while answering "why
does the openai arm show blank est. cost?" during the S10 live run.

I originally recorded this as "Anthropic rows silently unpriced while Bedrock prices fine". That is true
but UNDERSTATES it. Measured against the installed genai-prices with the same call shape `_price_row` uses:

    provider_id="anthropic", model_ref="anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"           -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="anthropic", model_ref="claude-sonnet-4-6"                     -> OK  $0.004500
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="openai:gpt-5.4"                        -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="gpt-5.4"                               -> OK  $0.004000
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="openai:gpt-5.4-mini"                   -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="gpt-5.4-mini"                          -> OK  $0.001200
    provider_id="bedrock",   model_ref="bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" -> OK  $0.004950
    control: provider_id="openai", model_ref="gpt-4o"                          -> OK  $0.003500

SO: **only the BEDROCK prefix form happens to resolve. Anthropic AND OpenAI both read blank.** The models
are all perfectly well known to genai-prices — the bare forms price fine. The id is simply malformed by the
`provider:` prefix that `_price_row` passes through as `model_ref`, and `LookupError` (genai-prices
unknown-model signal) is then caught at usage_log.py:429 and turned into "unpriced" with no warning.

WHY THIS IS MORE THAN COSMETIC, and worse for this epic specifically: the CI provider matrix
[rebar:f124-f14a-fd62-4973] exists to compare providers, and its cost table would show BEDROCK WITH
FIGURES AND THE OTHER TWO ARMS EMPTY. A reader would naturally conclude Bedrock is the expensive arm, when
in fact it is the only arm being measured at all. That is a wrong-direction bias in exactly the comparison
the epic was built to inform — and it is why f124s cost figures had to be computed BY HAND from logged
token counts rather than read off the tooling.

The observable symptom is the `est. cost excludes N unpriced calls` line in CI job summaries, on runs where
genai-prices demonstrably knows every model involved.

This does not change the approach: still a provider-aware id translation decided by REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP
rather than a `split(":")`, because the Bedrock remainder (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`) is not
genai-prices own AWS id shape either. It does raise the priority: the defect silently biases a
provider-cost comparison rather than merely omitting a number.

AC1 should be read as covering ALL THREE providers, not just Anthropic — a test that fixes only the
anthropic prefix would leave OpenAI blank and the bias intact.

# Usage-log pricing silently drops Anthropic and OpenAI rows: the provider-prefixed model_ref LookupErrors

## THIS IS A REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY THIS EPIC

Before the provider-seam work, the usage log recorded a BARE model id (`claude-opus-4-8`), which
genai-prices resolves, so Anthropic prices displayed correctly. This epic made model strings
PROVIDER-QUALIFIED, and `agent_call.py` records `model=ran_model` verbatim — so the stored id became
`anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`, which genai-prices cannot resolve. `ran_model`'s history runs through this
epic's own tickets: 747e149455 (2932, first-class Bedrock), cc33, e6bd, 8455, 5e75.

So the correct close class is `regression`, not `preexisting`, and this belongs INSIDE epic 061c rather
than beside it.

## Mechanism

`usage_log._price_row` (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:412) passes the STORED `provider:model` string as
`model_ref` to `genai_prices.calc_price`. When that id does not resolve, genai-prices raises
`LookupError` — its unknown-model signal — which `_price_row` catches at :429 and turns into "unpriced".
The catch is correct as a policy (pricing must never break `summarize`) but it makes the failure SILENT:
the row is dropped from the cost total with no warning, because `LookupError` is swallowed before the
`WARNING` branch.

## MEASURED against the installed genai-prices, using the same call shape as `_price_row`

    provider_id="anthropic", model_ref="anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"            -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="anthropic", model_ref="claude-sonnet-4-6"                      -> OK  $0.004500
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="openai:gpt-5.4"                         -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="gpt-5.4"                                -> OK  $0.004000
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="openai:gpt-5.4-mini"                    -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="gpt-5.4-mini"                           -> OK  $0.001200
    provider_id="bedrock",   model_ref="bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" -> OK  $0.004950
    control: provider_id="openai", model_ref="gpt-4o"                           -> OK  $0.003500

## The defect is ASYMMETRIC, and that is what makes it harmful rather than merely untidy

ONLY the `bedrock:` prefix form happens to resolve. Anthropic AND OpenAI both read blank. Every model
involved is well known to genai-prices — the bare forms all price. So a provider cost comparison shows
figures for Bedrock and nothing for the other two, which reads as "Bedrock is the expensive arm" when it
is in fact the only arm being measured. That is a wrong-direction bias in exactly the comparison this
epic exists to inform, and it is why the CI provider matrix's cost table
[rebar:f124-f14a-fd62-4973] had to be computed BY HAND from logged token counts.

## Blast radius is not limited to CI

`summarize` renders the "est. cost" column for `rebar usage` output generally
(src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:444), so ordinary local and review-bot cost reporting is affected too, not
only the external-integration job summary. The observable symptom is the
`est. cost excludes N unpriced calls` line on runs where genai-prices demonstrably knows every model.

## Approach

Pass genai-prices an id it can resolve, keeping `provider_id` as the provider signal it already is.

The naive fix — strip everything before the first `:` — is WRONG for Bedrock, whose remainder
(`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`) is not genai-prices' own AWS id shape either (its AWS ids look like
`regional.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6-v1:0`). So this needs a provider-aware translation, and per this
epic's standing decision it must be decided by REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP rather than prefix sniffing or a
`split(":")` — the attested guard
`test_capabilities_module_still_has_no_provider_name_prefix_matching` exists for exactly this class of
shortcut.

Do NOT remove the `LookupError` -> unpriced policy; pricing must stay best-effort and must never break
`summarize`. The fix is to stop feeding it an unresolvable id, and to make a genuinely-unknown model
visibly unpriced rather than indistinguishable from a mis-formatted one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An Anthropic usage row PRICES rather than silently dropping to unpriced, proven by a test that
      FAILS before the fix on a realistic stored row (`provider="anthropic"`,
      `model="anthropic:claude-..."`).
- [ ] An OpenAI usage row also prices — the fix covers ALL affected providers, not just Anthropic. A fix
      that handled only the `anthropic:` prefix would leave OpenAI blank and the comparison bias intact.
- [ ] A Bedrock usage row still prices, and the Anthropic/Bedrock rate relationship is asserted so the
      asymmetry cannot silently return.
- [ ] The id translation is decided by REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP, not by prefix matching or `split(":")`, and a
      test pins that — consistent with `capabilities.py`'s attested no-prefix-matching guard.
- [ ] A model genuinely unknown to genai-prices is still tolerated as unpriced (pricing never breaks
      `summarize`) and is DISTINGUISHABLE in output from a row dropped because its id was mis-formatted.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green; the config-read
      and env-drift gates pass.
